namespace OuterMeasure

/-- `OuterMeasure.pi m` is the finite product of the outer measures `{m i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be the maximal outer measure `n` with the property that
  `n (pi univ s) ≤ ∏ i, m i (s i)`, where `pi univ s` is the product of the sets
  `{s i | i : ι}`. -/
protected def pi (m : ∀ i, OuterMeasure (α i)) : OuterMeasure (∀ i, α i) :=
  boundedBy (piPremeasure m)

/-- `Measure.pi μ` is the finite product of the measures `{μ i | i : ι}`.
  It is defined to be measure corresponding to `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi`. -/
protected irreducible_def pi : Measure (∀ i, α i) :=
  toMeasure (OuterMeasure.pi fun i => (μ i).toOuterMeasure) (pi_caratheodory μ)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The Bochner integral -/
irreducible_def integral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → G) : G :=
  if _ : CompleteSpace G then
    if hf : Integrable f μ then L1.integral (hf.toL1 f) else 0
  else 0

/-- An auxiliary definition used only to construct the true `NormedAddCommGroup` (and `Metric`)
structure provided by `Matrix.instMetricSpaceL2Op` and `Matrix.instNormedAddCommGroupL2Op`. -/
@[instance_reducible]
def l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux : NormedAddCommGroup (Matrix m n 𝕜) :=
  @NormedAddCommGroup.induced ((Matrix m n 𝕜) ≃ₗ[𝕜] (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m)) _
    _ _ _ ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup.toNormedAddGroup _ _ <|
    (toEuclideanLin.trans toContinuousLinearMap).injective

/-- The norm structure on `Matrix m n 𝕜` arising from the operator norm given by the identification
with (continuous) linear maps of `EuclideanSpace`. -/
@[instance_reducible]
def instL2OpNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup (Matrix m n 𝕜) where
  norm := l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.norm
  dist_eq := l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.dist_eq

scoped[Matrix.Norms.L2Operator] attribute [instance] Matrix.instL2OpNormedAddCommGroup

lemma cstar_norm_def (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : ‖A‖ = ‖toEuclideanCLM (n := n) (𝕜 := 𝕜) A‖ := rfl

/-- This is the same as `Matrix.l2_opNNNorm_def`, but with a more bundled RHS for square

/-- `dotProduct v w` is the sum of the entrywise products `v i * w i`.

See also `dotProductEquiv`. -/
def dotProduct [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] (v w : m → α) : α :=
  ∑ i, v i * w i

namespace Matrix

/-- `M * N` is the usual product of matrices `M` and `N`, i.e. we have that
`(M * N) i k` is the dot product of the `i`-th row of `M` by the `k`-th column of `N`.
This is currently only defined when `m` is finite. -/
-- We want to be lower priority than `instHMul`, but without this we can't have operands with
-- implicit dimensions.
@[default_instance 100]
instance [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] :
    HMul (Matrix l m α) (Matrix m n α) (Matrix l n α) where
  hMul M N := fun i k => (fun j => M i j) ⬝ᵥ fun j => N j k

theorem mul_apply [Fintype m] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] {M : Matrix l m α} {N : Matrix m n α}
    {i k} : (M * N) i k = ∑ j, M i j * N j k :=
  rfl

instance [Fintype n] [Mul α] [AddCommMonoid α] : Mul (Matrix n n α) where
  mul M N := M * N

definition_kinds.meaning: The same original experiment of q+1 independent standard d-dimensional Gaussian columns; physical row i collects coordinate i of all columns as Euclidean(q+1)-space. All expectations use that exact product measure.

r=q+1; L=2r+3log(1000d); theta=(i.val+1-1/2)pi/d; feature0=1 and featurek=sqrt2cos(k theta). Yi is inverse-d times the actual-row outer product Kronecker feature outer product on the closed norm-squared cutoff, and zero outside. Paired indices are Gaussian-first in both positions.

Matrix is a finite two-entry function. The actual Mul instance is ordinary matrix multiplication: (MN)ij=sum_k Mik Nkj, not entrywise multiplication. Under Matrix.Norms.L2Operator the norm is the induced Euclidean operator norm. Actual NormedRing, NormedSpace and completeness instances are synthesized, not supplied.

Integrable means an almost-everywhere strongly measurable representative and finite extended-norm integral. Bochner integral defaults to zero outside complete/integrable cases. The explicit integrability conclusions for all squared variables prevent a vacuous second-moment bound from that default. Integrability of Yi and centered algebraic terms, and all finite-sum/integral exchanges required by the proof, must be established internally.

M is Hermitian (conjugate transpose M=M) and the quadratic form sum_i,j star(x_i) Mij x_j is nonnegative for every finitely supported x. Since the index set is finite, this is the usual finite-dimensional positive-semidefinite matrix condition. It is a conclusion, not an extra hypothesis. The displayed P difference expresses the Loewner upper bound.

mean_i is the actual Bochner expectation of Yi under mu; Zi=Yi-mean_i; wi=cos((2q+1)theta_i); C=2r(r+2)/d. No formal mean matrix, supplied variance, or symbolic random variable substitutes for these definitions.

Every actual Yi squared is integrable and C I minus the sum of their actual second moments is positive semidefinite. The source uncentered bound is a material input for the actual centered variance consumer.

Every Zi squared and every (wi Zi) squared is integrable. Both actual sums of centered second moments have Euclidean operator norm at most C. Hermitian/PSD facts, centered moment identity and weighted comparison needed to obtain these actual norm bounds are internal proof obligations.
